newsitem.title: USA: French 'copter sets off on trans-Atlantic flight.
newsitem.headline: French 'copter sets off on trans-Atlantic flight.

text.p: French pilots took off Friday to attempt the first non-stop trans-Atlantic flight by a single-engine helicopter.
The Eurocopter ASTAR 350 B3 helicopter piloted by Philippe Boutry, 45, and Gerard David, 55, lifted off from a small airfield at Teterboro, near New York, at about 2:15 p.m. EDT (1815 GMT).

David told reporters the flight was designed to display in-flight refueling equipment and techniques. The trip is being sponsored by Eurocopter Group and Intertechnique Group, a French flight equipment company.
The flight to Paris' Le Bourget airport was expected to take 27 hours.

The helicopter has special tanks and other equipment that allow for in-flight refueling from land or sea, and was scheduled to take on fuel five times -- at Fredericton, New Brunswick, and Gander, Newfoundland, and from tugs between Newfoundland and Europe.
Eurocopter is 70 percent owned by France's Ste Nationale Industrie Aerospatiale and 30 percent by Deutsche Aerospace.
The Atlantic has been flown non-stop several times by multi-engine helicopters that refueled en route.
